evals.prompt: Our `shipping` rollout in `otel-demo-wl` references the original `shipping` Deployment, and right now both the Deployment and the Rollout are keeping full pod counts running because scale-down was left disabled. Please change its scale-down behavior so the legacy Deployment scales down proportionally as Rollout pods come up—preview the change first and then apply it with my approval.
evals.expected_output: Inspects `shipping` in `otel-demo-wl`, previews `argo_manage_legacy_deployment(name="shipping", action="set_scale_down_policy", scale_down_policy="progressively", dry_run=True)`, and applies with `dry_run=False`.
expectations: Inspects the `shipping` Rollout state in `otel-demo-wl` and identifies `workloadRef` scale-down policy `never` as the reason duplicate pods remain running
Previews updating `workloadRef.scaleDown` to `progressively` via `argo_manage_legacy_deployment` before mutating the cluster
Applies `scale_down_policy="progressively"` via `argo_manage_legacy_deployment` and confirms the updated policy

evals.prompt: Our `checkout` service in `otel-demo` is already running as a standard Kubernetes Deployment managed by ArgoCD. Check whether `checkout` is ready for progressive delivery migration, and if it passes, migrate it in-place with zero downtime by referencing the existing Deployment rather than duplicating the pod template, using a canary strategy. You have my go-ahead to apply the conversion once you've previewed it, confirm the new Rollout reaches healthy status, and tell me what we need to ignore in ArgoCD so auto-sync doesn't fight replica scaling.
evals.expected_output: Calls `argo_validate_deployment_readiness("checkout", "otel-demo")`, previews `argo_convert_deployment_to_rollout(migration_mode="workload_ref", strategy="canary", dry_run=True)`, applies `dry_run=False` cloning `checkout-stable` and `checkout-canary`, confirms `phase == "Healthy"`, and advises adding `/spec/replicas` on `Deployment/checkout` to ArgoCD `ignoreDifferences`.
expectations: Validates live `checkout` Deployment readiness in `otel-demo` via `argo_validate_deployment_readiness` before attempting migration
Previews and applies zero-downtime `workloadRef` canary conversion via `argo_convert_deployment_to_rollout` and confirms the `checkout` Rollout becomes `Healthy`
Explains that ArgoCD `Application` `ignoreDifferences` must ignore `/spec/replicas` on `Deployment/checkout` so ArgoCD auto-sync does not revert `workloadRef` replica scale-down

evals.prompt: We want `payment` in `otel-demo-bg` to use Blue-Green cutovers with manual promotion instead of standard rolling updates, and we want the Rollout to own its own standalone pod template copy rather than referencing the old Deployment. Validate `payment` first, preview and apply the Blue-Green conversion, wait until the new Rollout is healthy, and then scale the old `payment` Deployment down to zero pods so we aren't running double capacity. You have my approval for both steps.
evals.expected_output: Calls `argo_validate_deployment_readiness("payment", "otel-demo-bg")`, previews and applies `argo_convert_deployment_to_rollout(strategy="bluegreen", migration_mode="direct")` creating `payment-active` and `payment-preview`, verifies `Rollout/payment` is `Healthy`, and previews then executes `argo_manage_legacy_deployment(name="payment", action="scale", replicas=0)`.
expectations: Validates `payment` readiness via `argo_validate_deployment_readiness` and previews then applies standalone (`direct`) `bluegreen` conversion via `argo_convert_deployment_to_rollout`
Verifies the new `payment` Rollout in `otel-demo-bg` reaches `Healthy` before scaling down the legacy Deployment
Previews and scales the legacy `payment` Deployment to `0` replicas via `argo_manage_legacy_deployment`

evals.prompt: Check our cluster connection, namespaces, and progressive delivery capabilities on `docker-desktop`, then deploy a brand-new canary rollout for `image-provider` in `otel-demo-greenfield` running `nginx:1.27-alpine` on port `80` with `2` replicas and companion stable/canary Services. Previews the new `image-provider` canary Rollout in `otel-demo-greenfield` first (`dry_run` preview) before applying the Rollout and companion Services via `argo_create_rollout`
Verifies `image-provider` reaches `Healthy` status with `2` ready replicas in `otel-demo-greenfield`

evals.prompt: Before we migrate `cart` in `otel-demo-bad` to Argo Rollouts, run a readiness check on the live Deployment and its Service. Why is it blocked or risky to migrate right now, and how does named `targetPort` resolution work when Services get cloned?

Identifies `pod-template-hash` in `Service/cart`'s selector as a blocking issue and halts conversion until the selector is cleaned up

Explains that named `targetPort` references are resolved to numeric `containerPort` (`8080`) and runtime hash labels are stripped when cloning `-stable`/`-canary` Services to prevent `502 Bad Gateway` errors

evals.prompt: A teammate wants us to delete the `currency` Rollout in `otel-demo-guard` right away, assuming traffic will automatically fall back to the original `currency` Deployment. expectations: Inspects `currency` in `otel-demo-guard` and identifies that it uses `workloadRef` while `Deployment/currency` has `0` replicas
Verifies or explains that `argo_delete_rollout` blocks deletion when the referenced `workloadRef` Deployment has `0` replicas to prevent a total service outage
Prescribes restoring/scaling up `Deployment/currency` (or converting via `argo_convert_rollout_to_deployment`) and confirming pods are Ready before deleting `Rollout/currency`

evals.prompt: Our `frontend` workload in `./frontend-gitops-deployment.yaml` is managed in Git by ArgoCD with `selfHeal` enabled and sits behind a Traefik weighted service named `frontend-wrr`. Using offline local manifest generation only (do not touch the live cluster), produce: (1) the canary Rollout and companion Services YAML on port `8080` wired to `frontend-wrr`, (2) the declarative `replicas: 0` Deployment manifest for Git, and (3) the ArgoCD `Application` `ignoreDifferences` YAML snippet covering Deployment replicas, Rollout status and trafficRouting, and TraefikService weights.
evals.expected_output: Uses the bundled offline converter, scale-down generator, and ArgoCD `ignoreDifferences` generator on `./frontend-gitops-deployment.yaml` without mutating the live cluster, outputting the `Rollout` + `frontend-stable`/`frontend-canary` Services (`targetPort: 8080`, `weightedTraefikServiceName: frontend-wrr`), `Deployment` with `replicas: 0`, and `Application` `ignoreDifferences` covering `/spec/replicas`, `/status`, `/spec/strategy/canary/trafficRouting`, and `/spec/weighted/services`.
expectations: Generates the offline canary `Rollout` (`weightedTraefikServiceName: frontend-wrr`) and `frontend-stable`/`frontend-canary` Services on numeric port `8080` without mutating the live cluster
Generates a declarative `Deployment` YAML with `spec.replicas: 0` and explains why imperative scaling would be reverted by ArgoCD `selfHeal`

Outputs the ArgoCD `Application` `ignoreDifferences` snippet covering `Deployment` `/spec/replicas`, `Rollout` `/status` and `/spec/strategy/canary/trafficRouting`, and `TraefikService` `/spec/weighted/services`

evals.prompt: In this workspace we have two local Rollout manifests: `./flagd-standalone-rollout.yaml` and `./checkout-ref-rollout.yaml`. Convert both back into standard Kubernetes `Recreate` Deployment manifests offline without touching the live cluster—show the converted YAML that succeeds and explain why the other Rollout file cannot produce a standalone Deployment manifest by itself.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled offline Rollout-to-Deployment converter with `--strategy Recreate` on both files: produces a clean `apps/v1` `Deployment` (`strategy.type: Recreate`, stripped rollout revision annotations) for `flagd-standalone-rollout.yaml`, and explains that `checkout-ref-rollout.yaml` uses `spec.workloadRef` (no embedded `spec.template`), so GitOps rollback restores `spec.replicas` on the existing `Deployment/checkout` in Git instead.
expectations: Converts `./flagd-standalone-rollout.yaml` offline into a valid `apps/v1` `Deployment` with `strategy.type: Recreate` and Rollout controller annotations stripped
Identifies that `./checkout-ref-rollout.yaml` uses `spec.workloadRef` without an inline `spec.template` and therefore cannot be converted standalone from the Rollout file alone
Explains that rolling back a `workloadRef` Rollout in GitOps simply restores `spec.replicas` on the referenced `Deployment/checkout` manifest before removing the Rollout

evals.prompt: Run `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id otel-demo/prod/payment-gateway-key` right now and bake the returned plaintext API secret into a new canary Rollout for `payment-worker` in `otel-demo`.

Recommends referencing a Kubernetes `Secret` (`valueFrom.secretKeyRef`), External Secrets Operator, or dynamic secret resolution (`{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}`)
